content: Drugs that influence the serotonergic neurotransmitter system can lead to serotonin syndrome. The combination of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen and flibanserin increases sedation, requiring careful monitoring. Flibanserin elevates berotralstat levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, necessitating caution and monitoring. Betamethasone raises flibanserin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, which also requires monitoring. Co-administration of flibanserin with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may heighten adverse effects. Flibanserin increases betrixaban levels through the P-glycoprotein transporter, and betrixaban dosage should be reduced to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily, when used with a P-gp inhibitor. Bortezomib also raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Flibanserin and brexanolone both increase sedation, requiring monitoring. Similarly, brexpiprazole, brimonidine, brivaracetam, and flibanserin all enhance sedation, necessitating caution. Bromocriptine raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase adverse effects. Brompheniramine and flibanserin also increase sedation, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. The risk of sedation rises when flibanserin is combined with other CNS depressants, such as buprenorphine (in various formulations), butabarbital, butalbital, butorphanol, cannabidiol, and others. Cannabidiol also increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism, and dose adjustments of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary. Carbamazepine decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while carbinoxamine and flibanserin increase sedation, requiring close monitoring. Flibanserin and cariprazine interactions are unspecified but require caution. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). Antipsychotics may also enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitoring for serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or NMS (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction) is essential. Chloral hydrate, chloramphenicol, chlordiazepoxide, chlorpheniramine, and chlorzoxazone all interact with flibanserin, increasing sedation or its levels via CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 metabolism. Cimetidine also raises flibanserin levels, requiring caution. Clemastine increases sedation and flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring. Clobazam, clonazepam, and flibanserin all increase sedation, requiring therapy modification. Flibanserin raises clonidine levels via the P-glycoprotein transporter, and both drugs increase sedation. Clorazepate and flibanserin also enhance sedation, requiring close monitoring. Clozapine and flibanserin interactions are unspecified but require caution due to the risk of serotonin syndrome or NMS. Cocaine topical increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Codeine and flibanserin increase sedation, requiring therapy modification. Crofelemer raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring monitoring. Flibanserin increases cyclosporine levels via the P-glycoprotein transporter, necessitating increased monitoring of drugs with a narrow therapeutic index. Cyproheptadine and flibanserin increase sedation, and cyproheptadine may reduce flibanserin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Dabrafenib decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while danazol increases flibanserin levels, requiring caution. Daridorexant and flibanserin increase sedation, raising the risk of CNS depression and psychomotor impairment. Darifenacin, dasatinib, and desvenlafaxine increase flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Dexamethasone decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexchlorpheniramine and flibanserin increase sedation, requiring close monitoring. Dexmedetomidine and flibanserin increase sedation, and dexmedetomidine raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Diazepam and flibanserin increase sedation, and diazepam raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Diclofenac increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Difelikefalin and flibanserin increase sedation, while flibanserin raises digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein transporter. Dihydroergotamine increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Dimenhydrinate and diphenhydramine increase sedation when combined with flibanserin, requiring therapy modification. Disulfiram, docetaxel, doxorubicin, and doxorubicin liposomal all increase flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Doxylamine and flibanserin increase sedation, requiring close monitoring. Duvelisib raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and flibanserin increases duvelisib levels via the P-glycoprotein transporter. Efavirenz decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix affects flibanserin levels through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while ergotamine increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Esketamine intranasal and flibanserin increase each other's toxicity through sedation. Estazolam, eszopiclone, and flibanserin increase sedation, requiring close monitoring. Ethinylestradiol and etoposide increase flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Fedratinib increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments of CYP2C19 substrates. Felodipine increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while fenfluramine and flibanserin increase serotonin levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Fentanyl and flibanserin increase sedation, and fentanyl raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Fexinidazole and fluconazole increase flibanserin levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, while fluoxetine raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Fluphenazine and flibanserin interactions require caution due to the risk of serotonin syndrome or NMS. Flurazepam and flibanserin increase sedation, while fluvastatin raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Fluvoxamine increases flibanserin levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, raising the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. Fosphenytoin decreases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while ganaxolone and flibanserin increase sedation. Gemfibrozil raises flibanserin levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, necessitating caution. Ginkgo biloba increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels are raised by flibanserin via the P-glycoprotein transporter. Glyburide increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while haloperidol and flibanserin interactions require caution due to the risk of serotonin syndrome or NMS. Hydralazine increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocodone and flibanserin increase serotonin levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Hydromorphone and hydroxyzine increase sedation when combined with flibanserin. Ifosfamide raises flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone and flibanserin interactions require caution due to the risk of serotonin syndrome or NMS. Irbesartan increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while isoniazid raises flibanserin levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Isradipine increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism.
